hints.content:
The key understanding here is that $\triangle WXY$ is similar to triangle $\boxed{1}$ based on the AA criterion (they both have a right angle and a $70\degree$ angle).

We can find $\dfrac{WY}{WX}$ by setting up a proportion statement that includes $WX$, $WY$,  and the lengths of their corresponding sides in triangle $\boxed{1}$.

options.alt: Two triangles. A right triangle W X Y. Angle Y is a right angle. Angle W is seventy degrees. The other triangle is labeled one and has its short leg labeled three point four units. Its long leg is nine point four units. Its hypotenuse is ten units. The angle opposite of the hypotenuse is ninety degrees. The angle opposite of the short leg is twenty degrees. The angle opposite of the long leg is seventy degrees.
